title: Two-Step Inequalities
short: Solve like an equation, but reverse the sign when you multiply or divide by a negative.
trouble: Students forget to reverse the inequality after dividing by a negative number.

blocks.html: An inequality like $3x - 4 > 11$ has many solutions. You can solve it almost exactly like a two-step equation, and graph the answer the way you graphed inequalities in Grade 6. There is one new rule.
Solve the way you would solve an equation. But when you multiply or divide both sides by a negative number, reverse the inequality sign ($<$ becomes $>$, $\le$ becomes $\ge$).

Adding or subtracting slides both sides the same way, so their order stays the same. Multiplying by a negative number flips the number line around $0$: $2 < 5$, but $-2 > -5$, because $-2$ is to the right of $-5$. So after multiplying or dividing by a negative, the bigger side becomes the smaller side, and the sign must turn around to stay true.

blocks.name: numberline
blocks.cap: $2 < 5$, but their opposites are in the other order: $-2 > -5$. Multiplying by $-1$ flips the order.

blocks.title: No flip needed
steps: Divide by 3 (positive, so the sign stays): $x > 5$.

blocks.title: Dividing by a negative
steps: Check $x = 4$: $-8 + 7 = -1 \le 1$ ✓. Check $x = 0$ (not in the answer): $7 \le 1$ is false ✓.

blocks.title: A word problem
blocks.q: You have \$40. A fair ticket costs \$12 and each ride costs \$3.50. How many rides can you take?
steps: Let $r$ be the number of rides: $12 + 3.5r \le 40$ ("at most \$40").
You can take at most 8 rides.

blocks.html: Forgetting to reverse the sign after dividing by a negative: $-2x \le -6$ becoming $x \le 3$. Test a number from your answer: $x = 0$ gives $7 \le 1$, which is false, so $x \le 3$ cannot be right. Testing one number catches this every time.
